mainTopic: The time limits for שחרית and מנחה according to רבי יהודה and the רבנן, the meaning of 'עד', the melting of the מן, and rules about davening near others.
overview: The amud opens by asking whether רבי יהודה's word 'עד' (until) includes the end point. Each reading seems to cause a problem. The גמרא solves this by explaining that פלג המנחה means 10¾ hours, so 'עד' can include the end point. רב נחמן then proves the point from רבי יהודה בן בבא's testimony that the morning תמיד was offered at four hours, and רב כהנא rules like רבי יהודה for שחרית. Next the גמרא asks whose view a ברייתא follows when it says the מן melted at four hours. It shows that both רבי יהודה and the רבנן can agree with it, and רבי אחא בר יעקב explains that four hours is when the sun is hot but the shade is still cool. For מנחה, רב חסדא finds no clear ruling, so a person may follow either opinion. A story about רב davening the שבת prayer early teaches three הלכות, including that one may not pass within four אמות in front of someone davening. The amud ends as the גמרא begins to challenge how רבי ירמיה could daven behind his teacher, and that challenge continues on the next amud.

steps.title: If 'until' is inclusive, רבי יהודה matches the רבנן
steps.stepSummary: The end of a challenge begun just before: if 'עד' includes the end point, רבי יהודה's limit for מנחה would be the same as the רבנן's.
steps.simpleTranslation: That is the same as the רבנן!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes a challenge it started just before: if 'עד פלג המנחה' includes the whole last half of the afternoon, רבי יהודה ends up saying exactly what the רבנן say.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The רבנן allow מנחה until evening. If 'until פלג המנחה' includes the entire second half of the afternoon, that half also ends at evening. Then there would be no argument at all, which cannot be right.

keyTerms.meaning: The Sages, the majority view in the משנה

phrases.english: That is the same as the Rabbis!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the challenge from the preceding text against reading 'עד' as inclusive.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading that 'עד' means up to and including (עד ועד בכלל).
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If inclusive, 'until פלג המנחה' runs to evening, which is the רבנן's position, so there would be no dispute.

steps.title: But the non-inclusive reading has its own problem: the end of the משנה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back: the alternative, that 'עד' is not inclusive, runs into trouble with the end of the משנה about מוסף.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, what are you saying, that 'until' does not include the end point? Look at the end of the משנה: The מוסף prayer may be said all day. רבי יהודה says: until seven hours.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא refuses to accept the last proof, because the other reading also causes a problem. It quotes the end of the משנה about מוסף to set up its next challenge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This step does not prove anything yet. It brings the relevant source: רבי יהודה says מוסף may be said 'until seven hours.' The real question is whether 'seven hours' includes the seventh hour itself, and the next steps use this to test the non-inclusive reading.

keyTerms.meaning: The additional prayer of שבת, ראש חודש and יום טוב

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the גמרא has decided that 'עד' is inclusive. It is just showing that the other reading also has a problem.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא מַאי, עַד וְלֹא עַד בַּכְּלָל?
phrases.english: Rather, what? 'Until' and not including?
Say the latter clause:
And the additional prayer: all day.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: עַד שֶׁבַע שָׁעוֹת.
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says: until seven hours.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא מַאי, עַד וְלֹא עַד בַּכְּלָל? אֵימָא סֵיפָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects drawing a conclusion from step 1 by turning to the alternative reading and quoting the סיפא of the משנה.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects treating step 1 as proof that 'עד' is not inclusive.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The non-inclusive reading will clash with the סיפא about מוסף, shown in the next steps.

steps.title: A ברייתא about choosing between מוסף and מנחה
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא discusses someone who must say both מוסף and מנחה. The רבנן put מנחה first because it is more frequent; רבי יהודה puts מוסף first because its time is about to run out.
steps.simpleTranslation: And a ברייתא taught: If a person had two prayers to say, one מוסף and one מנחה, he says מנחה first and then מוסף, because מנחה is frequent and מוסף is not. רבי יהודה says: he says מוסף first and then מנחה, because the time for מוסף is running out and the time for מנחה is not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא where a person needs to say both מוסף and מנחה at the same time, and asks which comes first. This is the evidence for the coming challenge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The רבנן follow the rule that something done more often (תדיר) comes first. רבי יהודה says מוסף comes first because its time is about to end. That means, according to רבי יהודה, there is a moment when מנחה's time has already started but מוסף's time has not yet finished.

keyTerms.meaning: Passing; its time is running out
A teaching from the time of the משנה that was not included in the משנה

steps.whyThisMatters: The idea that something more frequent comes first (תדיר ושאינו תדיר, תדיר קודם) is a general rule found throughout ש״ס.

phrases.english: And it was taught: If two prayers were before him,

phrases.aramaic: אַחַת שֶׁל מוּסָף וְאַחַת שֶׁל מִנְחָה —
phrases.english: one the additional prayer and one the afternoon prayer,

phrases.aramaic: מִתְפַּלֵּל שֶׁל מִנְחָה וְאַחַר כָּךְ שֶׁל מוּסָף,
phrases.english: he prays the afternoon prayer and afterward the additional prayer,
because this one is frequent, and that one is not frequent.
phrases.notes: מנחה is said every day; מוסף only on special days.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: מִתְפַּלֵּל שֶׁל מוּסָף
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says: He prays the additional prayer
and afterward the afternoon prayer,
because this one is passing, and that one is not passing.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a ברייתא to go along with the סיפא of the משנה quoted in step 2.
steps.raayaObject: That according to רבי יהודה the times for מוסף and מנחה overlap.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא of 'היו לפניו שתי תפלות'.

steps.title: Without an inclusive 'until,' מוסף and מנחה never overlap
steps.stepSummary: If 'until seven hours' stops at midday, the times for מוסף and מנחה (which starts at 6½ hours) never meet, so רבי יהודה's ruling in the ברייתא would be impossible.
steps.simpleTranslation: It works if you say 'until' includes the end point: then you can find a time when both prayers are due together. But if you say 'until' does not include the end point, how can both prayers ever be due together? Once מנחה's time arrives, מוסף's time is already gone!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the challenge. רבי יהודה's view in the ברייתא only works if 'until seven hours' includes the seventh hour.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מנחה begins at 6½ hours. If מוסף ends at the start of the seventh hour (midday), it ends before מנחה begins, so they never overlap. If 'until' includes the seventh hour, מוסף lasts until 7 hours, and from 6½ to 7 both are due. That is the situation the ברייתא describes.

keyTerms.meaning: It works well if you say
You can find them (such a case)

phrases.english: Granted, if you say 'until and including,'
that is how you find them,
two prayers together.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא אִי אָמְרַתְּ ״עַד וְלֹא עַד בַּכְּלָל״,
phrases.english: But if you say 'until and not including,'
how do you find them,
two prayers together?
Once the afternoon prayer has come,
the additional prayer has gone!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the sources from steps 2 and 3 to attack the non-inclusive reading.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading that 'עד' means up to but not including (עד ולא עד בכלל).
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: With a non-inclusive 'until,' מוסף ends at 6 hours and מנחה starts at 6½, so the overlap that the ברייתא assumes for רבי יהודה could never happen.

steps.title: Then the first clause is a problem again
steps.stepSummary: If 'עד' is inclusive, we are back to the first problem: what is the difference between רבי יהודה and the רבנן about מנחה?
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, what are you saying, that 'until' includes the end point? Then the first clause is difficult: what is the difference between רבי יהודה and the רבנן?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings back the original problem. The inclusive reading still seems to make רבי יהודה agree with the רבנן about מנחה, which sets up the answer that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now both readings have a problem. The inclusive reading fits the מוסף case but seems to erase the argument about מנחה. The גמרא now needs to solve this.

phrases.english: Rather, what? 'Until and including'?
The first clause is difficult:
phrases.notes: The first clause means the ruling about מנחה, 'until פלג המנחה.'

phrases.aramaic: מַאי אִיכָּא בֵּין רַבִּי יְהוּדָה לְרַבָּנַן?!
phrases.english: What is there between Rabbi Yehuda and the Rabbis?!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא מַאי, ״עַד וְעַד בַּכְּלָל״? קַשְׁיָא רֵישָׁא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After step 4 pushes toward the inclusive reading, this step brings back the problem from step 1.
steps.kashyaTarget: The inclusive reading of 'עד' in the רישא about מנחה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: An inclusive 'until פלג המנחה' seems to reach evening, which is the same as the רבנן.

steps.title: 'פלג המנחה' means the end of the first half, at 10¾ hours
steps.stepSummary: 'פלג המנחה' refers to the first half of the afternoon period. 'Until and including' that half means until 10¾ hours, not until evening. So 'עד' can be inclusive and רבי יהודה still disagrees with the רבנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: Do you think that 'פלג המנחה' refers to the second half? It refers to the first half. This is what it means: when does the first half end and the second half begin? From when eleven hours minus a quarter have passed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by explaining what 'פלג המנחה' really refers to. It means the first half of the late afternoon, which ends at 10¾ hours.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The late-afternoon period (מנחה קטנה) runs from 9½ hours to 12 hours, and its midpoint is 10¾ hours. The challenge assumed that 'until פלג' included the second half and so reached evening. But 'פלג' refers to the first half, so even 'until and including' ends at 10¾ hours, earlier than the רבנן's evening. Now 'עד' can be inclusive everywhere, both for מוסף and for מנחה.

keyTerms.meaning: The midpoint of the late-afternoon period, 10¾ hours after sunrise

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי יהודה, 'עד' means 'up to and including.' His מוסף lasts through the seventh hour, so it overlaps with מנחה. His מנחה ends at פלג המנחה, which is 10¾ hours, the end of the first half of the late afternoon.
steps.confusionAlert: פלג המנחה is not half of the whole afternoon. It is the midpoint of the late afternoon (9½ to 12 hours), which is 10¾ hours.
steps.whyThisMatters: The time 10¾ hours, פלג המנחה, is still the time used in practical הלכה, for example as the earliest time to daven מעריב and to light שבת candles according to רבי יהודה.

phrases.english: Do you think that this 'midpoint of the afternoon'
is speaking of the last half?
It is speaking of the first half,
and this is what it is saying:
When does the first half leave
and the last half enter?

phrases.aramaic: מִכִּי נָפְקִי אַחַת עֶשְׂרֵה שָׁעוֹת חָסֵר רְבִיעַ.
phrases.english: From when eleven hours minus a quarter have passed.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִי סָבְרַתְּ דְּהַאי ״פְּלַג מִנְחָה״ פְּלַג אַחֲרוֹנָה קָאָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 5, which allows the inclusive reading that step 4 requires.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining a term: 'פלג המנחה' refers to the first half, not the second.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Until פלג המנחה,' read inclusively, would include the second half and so reach evening, the same as the רבנן.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'Until and including' the first half ends at 10¾ hours, so רבי יהודה differs from the רבנן and 'עד' is consistently inclusive.

steps.title: רב נחמן brings a proof from the testimonies of רבי יהודה בן בבא
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן quotes a משנה in which רבי יהודה בן בבא testified about five things. The last is that the morning תמיד was once offered at four hours.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said: We also learned this in a משנה. רבי יהודה בן בבא testified about five things: that we may get a young girl to refuse her marriage; that we may let a woman remarry based on one witness; about a rooster that was stoned in ירושלים because it killed a person; about wine only forty days old that was poured on the altar; and about the morning תמיד that was offered at four hours.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן brings a משנה to support the idea from Step 6 that 'עד' includes the end-point. Only the last of the five testimonies matters for our question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Our משנה said, according to רבי יהודה, that שחרית may be said 'until four hours,' and תפלה matches the time of the תמיד. Here we hear that the morning תמיד was actually offered at four hours. This means the fourth hour itself still counts as valid time.

keyTerms.meaning: We also learned this (in a משנה): a phrase that introduces a supporting source
Testified (about a teaching he received from earlier teachers)
From מֵיאוּן: a young girl married off by her mother or brother may refuse the marriage
The daily morning offering in the בית המקדש

steps.confusionAlert: Do not try to connect all five testimonies to our topic. Four of them are simply quoted along with the rest of the משנה. Only the last one, about the תמיד, is the proof.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן: אַף אֲנַן נָמֵי תְּנֵינָא.
phrases.english: Rav Naḥman said: We too learned this in a mishna.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה בֶּן בָּבָא הֵעִיד חֲמִשָּׁה דְּבָרִים:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda ben Bava testified about five things:
that we may get a minor girl to refuse her marriage,

phrases.aramaic: וְשֶׁמַּשִּׂיאִין אֶת הָאִשָּׁה עַל פִּי עֵד אֶחָד,
phrases.english: and that we may let a woman remarry based on one witness,
phrases.notes: He means one witness who says her husband has died.

phrases.english: and about a rooster that was stoned in Jerusalem
because it killed a person,
and about wine forty days old
that was poured as a libation on the altar,
and about the daily morning offering
that was offered at four hours.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the answer of Step 6 that 'עד' includes the end-point.
steps.raayaObject: That 'עד ארבע שעות' includes the fourth hour (עד ועד בכלל).
steps.raayaSupportSource: משנה in עדיות: the testimony of רבי יהודה בן בבא that the morning תמיד was offered at four hours.

steps.title: Conclusion: 'until' includes the end-point
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא draws from the testimony that 'עד' means 'until and including,' and accepts this.
steps.simpleTranslation: Learn from this that 'until' means 'until and including.' Yes, learn from this.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא states the lesson of the proof and agrees with it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because the תמיד was valid during the fourth hour, the words 'until four hours' must include that hour. This settles the question that ran through Steps 2 to 6: 'עד' is inclusive.

keyTerms.meaning: Learn from this. When it is repeated, it means the גמרא accepts the proof.
Until and including: the end-point is part of the range

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי יהודה, שחרית may be said until the end of the fourth hour, because 'עד' includes the end-point.

phrases.english: Learn from this: 'until' means 'until and including.'
Indeed, learn from this.

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ עַד וְעַד בַּכְּלָל שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the conclusion from the proof in Step 7.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: 'עד' is inclusive, so רבי יהודה allows שחרית until the end of the fourth hour.

steps.title: רב כהנא rules like רבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: רב כהנא rules that the הלכה follows רבי יהודה, because a משנה in עדיות supports him.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב כהנא said: The הלכה follows רבי יהודה, since we learned a משנה in 'the chosen one' (עדיות) that agrees with him.
steps.whatsHappening: Now that the meaning is clear, רב כהנא gives the practical ruling: we follow רבי יהודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מסכת עדיות was taught with special authority, so a משנה there carries extra weight. Since the testimony about the תמיד at four hours matches רבי יהודה, the הלכה follows him over the רבנן.

keyTerms.meaning: The practical law follows this opinion
The chosen one: a name for מסכת עדיות
Like him, in agreement with him

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the practical deadline for שחרית: until the end of the fourth hour of the day.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב כָּהֲנָא: הֲלָכָה כְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה,
phrases.english: Rav Kahana said: The halakha follows Rabbi Yehuda,
since we learned in 'the chosen one' in agreement with him.
phrases.notes: 'The chosen one' is מסכת עדיות, the משנה we just quoted.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב כָּהֲנָא הֲלָכָה כְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns the proven meaning into a practical ruling.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The הלכה follows רבי יהודה: שחרית may be said until four hours.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The הלכה follows רבי יהודה because the משנה in עדיות supports him.

steps.title: Who taught that the מן melted at four hours?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא repeats the line about the תמיד at four hours and asks which תנא taught that the מן melted at four hours.
steps.simpleTranslation: About the morning תמיד that was offered at four hours: who is the תנא who taught that 'the sun grew hot and it melted' means four hours?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא repeats the last item of רבי יהודה בן בבא's testimony as a heading. Then it asks who taught a ברייתא saying the מן melted at four hours. This sets up the next move.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The testimony shows that 'morning' can stretch to four hours. That raises a question about the מן, which was gathered 'in the morning' and melted at four hours. The גמרא wants to know whose view of 'morning' this ברייתא follows.

keyTerms.meaning: The daily morning קרבן in the בית המקדש
Who is the תנא (who taught this)?
'And the sun grew hot and it melted' (about the מן)

phrases.english: And about the morning תמיד
phrases.notes: This is the last line of the testimony from step 7. The גמרא repeats it here as a heading.

phrases.english: that was offered at four hours.
Who is the תנא who taught this, which we learned:
"And the sun grew hot and it melted" means at four hours.
phrases.notes: שמות 16:21. The פסוק is about the מן, which was gathered in the morning and melted once the sun got hot.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the four-hour תמיד from the testimony as a springboard to examine a ברייתא about the מן.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which תנא's definition of 'morning' matches the ברייתא that the מן melted at four hours.

steps.title: The ברייתא proves the melting was at four hours, not six
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא shows that 'the sun grew hot' means four hours, because six hours already has its own phrase, 'the heat of the day.'
steps.simpleTranslation: You say four hours, but maybe it is six hours? Since the Torah already calls six hours 'the heat of the day,' I must explain 'the sun grew hot and it melted' as four hours.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the rest of the ברייתא. The ברייתא explains why the melting time is four hours and not noon.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah uses 'כחם היום' (the heat of the day) for six hours, which is noon. So a different phrase, 'וחם השמש,' must point to an earlier time, which is four hours.

keyTerms.meaning: 'In the heat of the day,' which is six hours (noon)
How do I explain (this other פסוק)?
Six hours into the day, which is midday

phrases.english: You say it was at four hours,
or perhaps it was only at six hours?!
When it says "in the heat of the day,"
six hours is already mentioned.
So how do I explain
"and the sun grew hot and it melted"? It means at four hours.

steps.triggerLanguage: אתה אומר בארבע שעות או אינו אלא בשש שעות
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the quote of the ברייתא that step 10 asked about.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: 'וחם השמש ונמס' refers to four hours, since six hours is already called 'כחם היום.'

steps.title: The ברייתא fits neither רבי יהודה nor the רבנן
steps.stepSummary: The מן was gathered in the morning and melted after morning ended, at four hours. Neither opinion ends morning before the fourth hour.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whose view is this? Not רבי יהודה and not the רבנן. For רבי יהודה, the time through four hours is still morning. For the רבנן, the time until noon is still morning.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the ברייתא. It argues that its timing does not match anyone's view of when 'morning' ends.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The מן was gathered 'בבקר,' in the morning, and melted when the morning was over. If melting is at four hours, morning must end before four. But רבי יהודה says morning runs through the fourth hour, and the רבנן say it runs until noon.
steps.confusionAlert: Remember from step 8 that 'עד' here means 'until and including.' So for רבי יהודה, the whole fourth hour still counts as morning.

phrases.aramaic: מַנִּי? לָא רַבִּי יְהוּדָה וְלָא רַבָּנַן.
phrases.english: Whose view is this? Neither רבי יהודה nor the רבנן.
If it is רבי יהודה,

phrases.aramaic: עַד אַרְבַּע שָׁעוֹת נָמֵי צַפְרָא הוּא!
phrases.english: until four hours is also still morning!

phrases.aramaic: אִי רַבָּנַן — עַד חֲצוֹת נָמֵי צַפְרָא הוּא.
phrases.english: If it is the רבנן, until noon is also still morning.

steps.triggerLanguage: מני לא רבי יהודה ולא רבנן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests the ברייתא from step 11 against both opinions about the תמיד.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא that the מן melted at four hours.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Melting marks the end of 'morning,' but both רבי יהודה (through four hours) and the רבנן (until noon) have morning lasting past the start of the fourth hour.

steps.title: Answer according to the רבנן: split the morning in two
steps.stepSummary: The doubled word 'בבקר בבקר' divides the morning into two halves. The מן was gathered only in the first half.
steps.simpleTranslation: You can say it follows רבי יהודה, or you can say it follows the רבנן. According to the רבנן: the פסוק says 'בבקר בבקר,' which means divide it into two mornings.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the ברייתא can fit either opinion. It starts by explaining how it fits the רבנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For the רבנן, morning is six hours. The doubled 'בבקר' cuts it into two mornings of three hours each. The מן was gathered in the first one, so by the fourth hour it was melting.

keyTerms.meaning: If you want, say (one possible answer)
'Morning by morning,' a doubled word in the פסוק

phrases.english: If you want, say it follows רבי יהודה,
and if you want, say it follows the רבנן.
If you want, say it follows the רבנן:
the פסוק says "morning by morning,"
divide it into two mornings.

steps.triggerLanguage: אי בעית אימא רבי יהודה אי בעית אימא רבנן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 12, starting with the רבנן.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reading an extra word in the פסוק to narrow the time of gathering
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The מן was gathered for the whole 'morning,' which for the רבנן lasts until noon.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'בבקר בבקר' splits the six-hour morning, so gathering ended after three hours and melting was at four.

steps.title: Answer according to רבי יהודה: the extra 'morning' moves it one hour earlier
steps.stepSummary: For רבי יהודה, the extra 'בקר' ends the gathering time one hour earlier than his normal morning.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you want, say it follows רבי יהודה: this extra 'morning' comes to make it one hour earlier.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows how the ברייתא can also fit רבי יהודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי יהודה, morning runs through four hours. The extra word 'בקר' moves the end of gathering one hour earlier, to three hours. That leaves the fourth hour as the time of melting.

phrases.english: And if you want, say it follows רבי יהודה:
this extra "morning"
comes to make it one hour earlier.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the second option promised in step 13, this time for רבי יהודה.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reading an extra word in the פסוק as shifting the time
steps.terutzHavaAmina: For רבי יהודה, gathering would last through the fourth hour.
steps.terutzMaskana: The extra 'בקר' ends gathering one hour sooner, so melting happens at four hours.

steps.title: Everyone agrees the melting was at four hours
steps.stepSummary: Whichever answer you use, both opinions agree that 'the sun grew hot and it melted' is at four hours.
steps.simpleTranslation: In any case, everyone agrees that 'the sun grew hot and it melted' is at four hours.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sums up the two answers. Both רבי יהודה and the רבנן agree on the four-hour melting time.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The argument about how long 'morning' lasts does not change the melting time. Each side reaches four hours through its own reading of 'בבקר בבקר.'

keyTerms.meaning: At any rate, in any case

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא about the מן fits both opinions. Everyone agrees the מן melted at four hours.

phrases.english: In any case, according to everyone,
"and the sun grew hot and it melted" is at four hours.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Wraps up the two answers of steps 13 and 14.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Both רבי יהודה and the רבנן place the melting of the מן at four hours.

steps.title: How do we know it means four hours?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks where in the פסוק the four-hour time comes from.
steps.simpleTranslation: How does the פסוק show this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the source in the פסוק that points to four hours. This sets up רבי אחא בר יעקב's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא only proved 'not six hours.' Now the גמרא wants a positive reason why the time is exactly four hours.

keyTerms.meaning: What shows this? How is it implied?

phrases.english: How does it show this?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the textual basis of the agreed four-hour time.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which word in 'וחם השמש ונמס' points to exactly four hours.

steps.title: רבי אחא בר יעקב: the sun is hot but the shade is still cool
steps.stepSummary: 'The sun grew hot' points to a time when the sun is hot but the shade is still cool. That is four hours.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אחא בר יעקב said: the פסוק says 'the sun grew hot and it melted.' At what hour is the sun hot but the shade still cool? You must say at four hours.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אחא בר יעקב answers the question. The פסוק says only the 'sun' was hot, which fits four hours.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says only the sun was hot, not the whole day. That means the shade was still cool. That happens at four hours, before noon, when even the shade gets hot.

keyTerms.meaning: You must say, this must be

steps.whatToRemember: Four hours is when the sun is hot but the shade is still cool. Six hours (noon) is when everything is hot, 'כחם היום.'

phrases.english: רבי אחא בר יעקב said:
the פסוק says "and the sun grew hot and it melted."
Which is the hour
when the sun is hot but the shade is cool?
You must say at four hours.

steps.triggerLanguage: אמר רבי אחא בר יעקב אמר קרא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly answers the question of step 16.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'וחם השמש' means only the sun is hot while the shade is cool, which happens at four hours.

steps.title: Is the הלכה like רבי יהודה for מנחה too?
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא asks רב יצחק: for שחרית, רב כהנא ruled like רבי יהודה. What is the ruling for מנחה?
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'מנחה may be said until evening, etc.' רב חסדא said to רב יצחק: There, about שחרית, רב כהנא said the הלכה follows רבי יהודה, because a משנה in the 'chosen' tractate agrees with him. Here, about מנחה, what is the ruling?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the משנה's line about מנחה. רב חסדא asks which opinion the הלכה follows for the end time of מנחה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For שחרית we already have a ruling like רבי יהודה, because עדיות backs him up. For מנחה, the רבנן say 'until evening' and רבי יהודה says 'until פלג המנחה.' רב חסדא wants to know whether the שחרית ruling carries over to מנחה.

phrases.english: The afternoon prayer until the evening, etc.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב חִסְדָּא לְרַב יִצְחָק:
phrases.english: Rav Chisda said to Rav Yitzchak:
There, Rav Kahana said
phrases.notes: 'There' means the ruling about שחרית, which can be said until four hours.

phrases.english: the halacha is like Rabbi Yehuda,
since we learned in the chosen tractate like him,
phrases.notes: The 'chosen' tractate is עדיות. Its rulings were treated as the accepted הלכה.

phrases.english: here, what is the ruling?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic on the משנה's line about מנחה
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the הלכה for the end time of מנחה follows רבי יהודה or the רבנן

steps.title: רב יצחק stays silent
steps.stepSummary: רב יצחק gives no answer at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: He was silent and did not say anything to him.
steps.whatsHappening: The question is met with silence. רב יצחק had no ruling to give.
steps.deeperAnalysis: No tradition about the הלכה is known, so in the next step רב חסדא tries to work it out himself. Step 22 gives the final outcome.

phrases.aramaic: אִישְׁתִּיק וְלָא אֲמַר לֵיהּ וְלָא מִידֵּי.
phrases.english: He was silent and did not say anything to him at all.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִישְׁתִּיק וְלָא אֲמַר לֵיהּ וְלָא מִידֵּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The response to the question in step 18: no answer
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: No answer is given, because no ruling is known

steps.title: Proof from רב davening the שבת prayer early
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא proves the הלכה follows רבי יהודה, since רב davened the שבת prayer on ערב שבת while it was still day.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said: Let us see for ourselves. Since רב davened the שבת prayer on ערב שבת while it was still day, learn from this that the הלכה is like רבי יהודה.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא tries to answer his own question from what רב actually did.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Davening מעריב of שבת before dark means the time for מנחה was already over. That only works if מנחה ends at פלג המנחה, which is רבי יהודה's view.

phrases.english: Rav Chisda said: Let us see for ourselves,
from the fact that Rav would daven the Shabbat prayer
on Erev Shabbat while it was still day,
learn from this that the halacha is like Rabbi Yehuda.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tries to answer the open question from step 18
steps.raayaObject: The הלכה follows רבי יהודה for מנחה
steps.raayaSupportSource: רב's practice of davening the שבת prayer early on ערב שבת

steps.title: On the contrary: רב הונא waited until night
steps.stepSummary: The proof is pushed back. רב הונא and the רבנן did not daven until night, which shows the הלכה is not like רבי יהודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: On the contrary! Since רב הונא and the רבנן would not daven until night, learn from this that the הלכה is not like רבי יהודה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers one practice with an opposite practice.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב הונא and the other students waited until dark to daven מעריב. That fits the רבנן, who say מנחה lasts until evening. So רב's practice proves nothing for certain.

phrases.english: On the contrary, from the fact that Rav Huna and the Rabbis
would not daven until nightfall,

phrases.aramaic: שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ אֵין הֲלָכָה כְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה.
phrases.english: learn from this that the halacha is not like Rabbi Yehuda.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof in step 20 with an opposite practice
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the proof from רב's practice
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Other great figures acted the opposite way, so one practice cannot decide the הלכה

steps.title: Either opinion may be followed
steps.stepSummary: Since no ruling was given, whoever follows either opinion has acted properly.
steps.simpleTranslation: Now that the הלכה was not stated like this master or like that master, one who acts like this master has acted properly, and one who acts like that master has acted properly.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא ends the discussion: there is no fixed ruling, so a person may choose.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Following רבי יהודה means davening מנחה until פלג המנחה, after which you may daven מעריב. Following the רבנן means davening מנחה until evening. Either way is valid.

keyTerms.meaning: Not like this master and not like that master
One who acts like a master has acted properly

steps.whatToRemember: There is no fixed ruling between רבי יהודה and the רבנן on when מנחה ends. A person may follow either one.
steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא itself does not discuss mixing the two opinions on the same day. The point is only that each opinion is a valid path to follow.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source for the choice people make today about davening מעריב early, after פלג המנחה.

phrases.english: Now that the halacha was not stated
not like this master and not like that master,
one who acted like this master has acted properly,
and one who acted like that master has acted properly.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Settles the standoff between steps 20 and 21
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: There is no binding ruling. Following either רבי יהודה or the רבנן is valid.

steps.title: רב davens early at גניבא's house
steps.stepSummary: A story: רב davened the שבת prayer on ערב שבת at גניבא's house. רבי ירמיה בר אבא was davening behind him, and רב did not step back and interrupt him.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב visited the house of גניבא and davened the שבת prayer on ערב שבת. רבי ירמיה בר אבא was davening behind רב. רב finished, but he did not interrupt רבי ירמיה's prayer.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story. It is setting up the next step, where three הלכות are learned from it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Three details matter here. רב davened early, a student davened right behind his teacher, and רב did not step back into the student's space after finishing.

phrases.english: Rav happened to come to the house of Geniva
and davened the Shabbat prayer on Erev Shabbat,

phrases.aramaic: וַהֲוָה מְצַלֵּי רַבִּי יִרְמְיָה בַּר אַבָּא
phrases.english: and Rabbi Yirmeya bar Abba was davening
behind Rav,
and Rav finished
and did not interrupt the prayer of Rabbi Yirmeya.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a story that also touches on davening the שבת prayer early
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב davened early and did not step back into the space of the student davening behind him

steps.title: Three lessons from the story
steps.stepSummary: Three הלכות are learned from the story: one may daven the שבת prayer on ערב שבת, a student may daven behind his teacher, and one may not pass in front of people who are davening.
steps.simpleTranslation: Learn three things from this. Learn that a person may daven the שבת prayer on ערב שבת. Learn that a student may daven behind his teacher. And learn that it is forbidden to pass in front of people who are davening.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pulls three practical lessons out of the story.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each lesson comes from one detail. The first comes from רב davening early. The second comes from רבי ירמיה davening behind רב. The third comes from רב not stepping back in front of him.

keyTerms.meaning: It is forbidden to pass in front of those davening

steps.whatToRemember: Three הלכות: davening the שבת prayer early is allowed, a student may daven behind his teacher, and one may not pass in front of someone davening.

phrases.english: Learn three things from this:
learn from this that a person may daven
the Shabbat prayer on Erev Shabbat.

phrases.aramaic: וּשְׁמַע מִינַּהּ מִתְפַּלֵּל תַּלְמִיד אֲחוֹרֵי רַבּוֹ.
phrases.english: And learn from this that a student may daven behind his teacher.

phrases.aramaic: וּשְׁמַע מִינַּהּ אָסוּר לַעֲבוֹר כְּנֶגֶד הַמִּתְפַּלְּלִין.
phrases.english: And learn from this that it is forbidden to pass in front of those who are davening.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the lessons from the story in step 23
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Three הלכות about davening are learned from רב's actions

steps.title: This supports רבי יהושע בן לוי
steps.stepSummary: The third lesson supports רבי יהושע בן לוי, who said it is forbidden to pass in front of people who are davening.
steps.simpleTranslation: This supports רבי יהושע בן לוי, because רבי יהושע בן לוי said: It is forbidden to pass in front of those who are davening.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that the story backs up a known statement of an אמורא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהושע בן לוי stated this rule on his own. רב's behavior in the story is real-life support for it.

phrases.aramaic: מְסַיַּיע לֵיהּ לְרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי.
phrases.english: This supports Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi.
As Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said:
It is forbidden to pass in front of those who are davening.

steps.triggerLanguage: מְסַיַּיע לֵיהּ לְרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Links the third lesson to an existing statement
steps.raayaObject: רבי יהושע בן לוי's rule that one may not pass in front of people davening
steps.raayaSupportSource: רב's behavior in the story at גניבא's house

steps.title: But רבי אמי and רבי אסי did pass
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the rule: רבי אמי and רבי אסי did pass in front of people davening.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is that so? But רבי אמי and רבי אסי did pass in front of people davening!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the rule by pointing to great חכמים who seemed to break it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If passing were forbidden, רבי אמי and רבי אסי would not have done it. So their behavior seems to argue against the rule.

phrases.english: Is that so?!

phrases.aramaic: וְהָא רַבִּי אַמֵּי וְרַבִּי אַסִּי חָלְפִי.
phrases.english: But Rabbi Ami and Rabbi Asi would pass!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the rule just supported in step 25
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule that one may not pass in front of people davening
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי אמי and רבי אסי passed in front of people davening, which shows it is allowed

steps.title: They passed beyond four אמות
steps.stepSummary: רבי אמי and רבי אסי passed only at a distance of more than four אמות from the people davening.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אמי and רבי אסי passed only outside of four אמות.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by narrowing where the rule applies.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ban is only on passing within four אמות in front of someone davening. Passing farther away than that is allowed, so the rule still stands.
steps.whatToRemember: The ban on passing in front of someone davening applies within four אמות.

phrases.english: Rabbi Ami and Rabbi Asi:
it was outside of four amos that they would pass.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 26
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits the case: the rule applies only within four אמות
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Their passing seemed to show there is no ban at all
steps.terutzMaskana: The ban covers only four אמות in front of the person davening. רבי אמי and רבי אסי passed farther away.

steps.title: How could רבי ירמיה daven behind his teacher?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא questions how רבי ירמיה could daven behind רב. It starts quoting a rule from רב, reported by רב יהודה, that begins: 'A person should never daven...'
steps.simpleTranslation: How could רבי ירמיה do that? Didn't רב יהודה say in the name of רב: 'A person should never daven...'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is surprised that רבי ירמיה davened behind his teacher, and it starts quoting a rule of רב to challenge him. This step only sets up the challenge. The rest of רב's rule comes in the next line.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 24 we learned that a student may daven behind his teacher. Now the גמרא pushes back on that lesson, because רב himself seems to have taught a rule limiting where a person may daven. The irony is sharp: the challenge uses רב's own words against something done right behind רב.

keyTerms.meaning: How could he do this? An expression of surprise at someone's behavior
But didn't [so-and-so] say? Opens a challenge from a known teaching

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the challenge is complete yet. The quote is cut off in the middle, so wait for the next line to see exactly what רב forbade.

phrases.english: And רבי ירמיה, how could he act this way?!
phrases.notes: 'This way' means davening behind his teacher רב, from the story in step 23.

phrases.aramaic: וְהָא אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב:
phrases.english: But didn't רב יהודה say that רב said:
A person should never daven

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי יִרְמְיָה הֵיכִי עָבֵיד הָכִי וְהָא אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After resolving the challenge to the third lesson about passing in front of people davening (steps 26-27), the גמרא turns to challenge the second lesson, that a student may daven behind his teacher.
steps.kashyaTarget: The lesson from step 24 that a student may daven behind his teacher, based on רבי ירמיה davening behind רב.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רב himself, as reported by רב יהודה, taught a rule beginning 'A person should never daven...'. The rest of the rule, given in the next line, seems to forbid what רבי ירמיה did, so his conduct looks like it goes against רב's own teaching.
